text:
Ava: hey — nightly eval alert for `qa_promptset_v2` showed a sudden quality drop overnight, +7% failure rate. outputs look more "noisy"/extra tokens. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/evals/nightly/qa_promptset_v2
MLNightlyBot: automated run 1825001234 posted. model: rdlw-v1.3-quant-int8, sampling config: temp=0.8 top_p=0.92 top_k=None seed=None
Kai: can someone repro locally? which exact binary / runtime? want to rule out serving vs model artifact
Ava: running on dedicated devbox (cuda12, runtime 2.7.1), model tgz from s3://redwood/models/rdlw-v1.3/2026-02-14/int8.tar
Riley: quick thought — quantization sometimes changes logits scale slightly, that can nudge cumulative probs and change top_p behavior. also float32->float16 rounding can move cutoffs.
Devon: do we have a logits histogram from the failing runs? ema mean/var would help
Ava: pasted quick dump:
```
Sample logits (first 8 tokens): [ -1.23, -0.95, -2.10, -0.11, -0.05, -3.0, -0.87, -0.12 ]
softmax probs (float32): [0.079,0.100,0.038,0.205,0.211,0.028,0.106,0.205]
cumsum: [0.079,0.179,0.217,0.422,0.633,0.661,0.767,0.972]
selected top_p=0.92 -> cutoff token index 7 (keeps 8 tokens)

Same prompt on float32 non-quant model:
probs: [0.080,0.101,0.037,0.206,0.212,0.027,0.105,0.210]
cumsum: [0.080,0.181,0.219,0.425,0.637,0.664,0.769,0.979]
cutoff index 6 (keeps 7 tokens)
```
Riley: small deltas but enough to flip decisions. top_p is brittle at that threshold edge. note the quantized run has slightly lower tail mass, but actually cumsum flips earlier in non-quant. weird.
Kai: did the nightly run set `seed=None`? nondeterministic sampling will amplify small numeric diffs
Ava: yes nightly uses unset seed to sample variety. but this regression is consistent across 8 runs overnight.
Devon: let's check how we compute top_p: are we doing cumulative sum in float32 or float64? and do we sort by logits then softmax? ordering + precision matters.
Riley: current code in runtime (serve/sampling/top_p.py) uses np.float32 for perf reasons. I can test switching to float64 for cumsum and comparator.
Kai: quick reproducer I ran:
```
python -m evals.run --model rdlw-v1.3-quant-int8 \
  --prompt examples/qa_sample.json --seed 1234 --temp 0.8 --top_p 0.92 --n 50
```
Results: 34/50 generated variants include the extra trailing token we flagged.
Ava: I also tried forcing `subtract_max=True` explicitly before softmax and that reduces flips but doesn't eliminate them.
Riley: hypothesis: quant kernel applies a small multiplicative scale (≤1.0008) to logits during dequant -> that shifts softmax tail and changes top_p cutoff. I'd expect differences at boundaries.
Devon: mitigation options:
- short-term: change nightly eval config to use seeded sampling (seed fixed) or switch to top_k for baseline comparisons
- medium: change cumsum to float64 and re-run tests
- long-term: fix quant kernel to preserve scale and add unit tests for top_p stability
Kai: I'll open PR to cast probs to float64 before np.cumsum and add a unit test that compares quant vs float baseline for boundary prompts (assert cutoff same or within tolerance). also adding a flag to force seeded nightly.
Ava: sounds good. for immediate false-positive relief, can we pin nightly to seed=42 and add a small hysteresis in alerting (ignore regressions <5%)? @MLNightlyBot team
MLNightlyBot: noted. created ticket RNW-ml/456: "pin nightly sampling seed + add alert hysteresis". will apply after review.
Riley: one more note — quantized model used a new exporter from the compile job (hash abcdef3). compare with previous exporter (abcdef2) — compile changed aten->custom kernel ordering. worth bisecting.
Devon: action items:
- Kai: PR for float64 cumsum + tests (ETA: today)
- Riley: run compile-bisect between abcdef2 & abcdef3 and report scale factor (ETA: tomorrow)
- Ava: change nightly config to seed=42 + 5% hysteresis (ETA: in prod today)
- MLNightlyBot: ignore noise alerts until change deployed
Ava: thanks all. feel free to drop short notes here if you find any quick reproducer snippets. :thumbsup:
Kai: on it. will link PR once ready.
Riley: I pushed a tiny script that prints logits scale diff: https://internal.redwood/repos/rdlw/quant-checks/compare_scale.py
Devon: added RNW-ml/457 to track quant kernel fix
Ava: closing loop later today after PR + nightly rerun, appreciate the quick triage :rocket:
